stories.title: Artemis Real Estate Buys Newport Beach, Calif., Senior Living Community From Ventas
stories.excerpt: Artemis Real Estate Partners has acquired a luxury senior living community in Newport Beach, Calif., from an affiliate of health care real estate investment trust Ventas, property records show. The Chevy Chase, Md.-based investment firm acquired Atria Newport Beach, a 168-unit senior living community at 393 Hospital Road, for $88.5 million, or $526,785 per unit. The property sits near Newport Boulevard and Hoag Hospital in one of Orange County’s most affluent coastal communities. Atria Senior Living partnered with the buyer in the transaction and will continue operating the community. JLL Capital Markets announced that it arranged the sale, including acquisition financing, but did not identify either the buyer or the seller, or disclose the value of the deal. The brokerage represented the seller. It did not disclose the amount of debt from an unidentified life insurance company. The property comprises two three-story buildings completed or renovated in 2021 and 2023. The studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom units include 126 independent living and assisted living units and 42 memory care units. Amenities include dining venues, a movie theater, a fitness center, a library, and a salon and spa, as well as concierge services. The transaction follows a $52 million refinancing in August 2024. JLL’s Aaron Rosenzweig and Dan Baker represented the seller in the latest transaction and arranged the acquisition financing. Artemis invests in senior housing, medical offices, multifamily, industrial and hospitality properties, while Ventas is one of the country’s largest publicly traded health care real estate owners. Neither firm was immediately available for contact. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Artemis Real Estate acquired 168-unit Atria Newport Beach from Ventas affiliate for $88.5M ($526.8K/unit)
Senior living asset in affluent Orange County coastal market, recently renovated (2021–2023)
Ventas portfolio rotation signals continued REIT repositioning toward core healthcare real estate
stories.summary: Artemis Real Estate Partners bought Atria Newport Beach, a 168-unit luxury senior living community in Orange County, Calif., from a Ventas affiliate for $88.5 million ($526,785 per unit). The property comprises two recently renovated buildings (2021–2023) with independent living, assisted living, and memory care units near Hoag Hospital in one of Orange County's most affluent communities. JLL Capital Markets arranged the sale and acquisition financing from an unnamed life insurance company.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact; this is healthcare-focused senior living. However, Ventas's asset sales signal REIT capital redeployment and potential dislocation in high-coastal-value real estate markets. Monitor for similar healthcare REIT portfolio pruning that may free up prime land for multifamily conversion in Orange County.

stories.title: Welltower Pays at Least $49M for Broward Rehab and Nursing Home
stories.excerpt: Health care real estate investment trust Welltower paid at least $49.1 million for a rehab and nursing home in suburban Broward County, Fla., property records show. Called Glades West Rehab & Nursing Center, the 86,009-square-foot complex features 120 beds in Miramar. Completed in 2015, the facility sits on a 3.7-acre site at 15955 Bass Creek Road, adjacent to Southwest 160th Avenue, just west of Interstate 75. The sale — which marks the first time the property was sold — equates to just over $409,000 per bed. The sale price, though, is likely higher than what’s listed in property records to account for the facility’s furniture and business operations. David Katz of Brooklyn-based TL Management sold the asset. In recent months, Welltower has been buying and selling South Florida properties. Since last year, the Toledo, Ohio-based firm has spent just under $170 million buying a 141-unit complex in Aventura, one spanning 22 acres in Lake Worth, and a third with 220 beds in Davie. In February, the company also sold a five-property portfolio in Palm Beach County for $81 million. In total, Welltower’s portfolio includes more than 2,500 facilities across the U.S., United Kingdom and Canada. Katz could not be reached for comment, while a spokesperson for Welltower did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Welltower acquired 120-bed Glades West nursing home in Miramar, Broward for $49.1M ($409K/bed)
First sale of property since 2015 completion; Welltower spent $170M on South Florida healthcare acquisitions in past 12 months
REIT aggressive buyer signals healthcare real estate capital availability and operator consolidation in South Florida
stories.summary: Welltower, a healthcare REIT based in Toledo, Ohio, paid at least $49.1 million for Glades West Rehab & Nursing Center, a 120-bed, 86,009-square-foot facility in Miramar, Broward County, Fla., completed in 2015. The purchase equates to just over $409,000 per bed. Over the past year, Welltower has deployed nearly $170 million acquiring healthcare properties across South Florida, including a 141-unit complex in Aventura, a 22-acre property in Lake Worth, and a 220-bed facility in Davie.
stories.impact: Welltower's continued South Florida healthcare acquisition blitz signals available debt capital and operator confidence in market fundamentals, but diverts institutional capital from multifamily. Monitor South Florida multifamily markets for potential wage/employment tailwinds from healthcare sector job creation and migration, offsetting any capital competition.

stories.title: Blackstone Provides $310M Bridge Loan for Nashville Mixed-Use Tower
stories.excerpt: A joint venture among PGIM, Stiles Corporation and Hensler Development has secured $310 million to refinance Peabody Union, a 665,000-square-foot office and residential development in Downtown Nashville, Tenn., according to JLL. Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies provided the debt, structured as a three-year bridge loan with two one-year extension options, while a JLL Capital Markets team of Ed Coco, Paul Stasaitis, Matt Casey, Anthony Sansone, Kelsey Bawcombe and Streeter Simmons arranged the transaction. Coco called Peabody Union “one of the most compelling mixed-use financing opportunities in the Southeast.” The asset has secured an office lease commitment from Starbucks that begins next year and will encompass nearly 250,000 square feet, Coco said. “We had a significant amount of interest from a variety of lender types,” he added. Located at 30-50 Peabody Street in Downtown Nashville’s South Bank district, a live-work-play neighborhood along the Cumberland River, Peabody Union recently finished construction and stands 27 stories. The mixed-use asset also features 355 luxury residential units and 52,735 square feet of experiential retail that opens next year. The building also includes two 2,000-square-foot outdoor terraces on the sixth floor, a 4,500-square-foot fitness and wellness center, a 4,000-square-foot club room for residents, and 1,000 square feet of bike storage. PGIM and Stiles did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commericialobserver.com.
bullets: Blackstone provided $310M three-year bridge loan (plus two 1-year extensions) for 665K-sf mixed-use tower in Nashville
Peabody Union (27-story, 665K sf) has locked 250K-sf Starbucks lease commencing next year; recently completed construction
Downtown Nashville mixed-use refinancing signals strong lender appetite for office-residential convergence and anchor tenant strength
stories.summary: A joint venture of PGIM, Stiles Corporation, and Hensler Development secured $310 million in bridge financing from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies to refinance Peabody Union, a newly completed 27-story, 665,000-square-foot mixed-use tower in Downtown Nashville's South Bank district. The asset has secured a significant lease commitment from Starbucks (nearly 250,000 sq ft, beginning next year). The three-year bridge includes two one-year extension options. JLL Capital Markets arranged the transaction.
stories.impact: Mixed-use financing momentum in Nashville signals strong office-plus-residential demand in a Sunbelt primary market experiencing sustained migration. The Starbucks anchor validates downtown positioning and creates high-traffic draw for residential units. Nashville's growth trajectory (tech, healthcare, entertainment) remains favorable for multifamily development; monitor office-to-residential conversion opportunities as office-only assets face headwinds.

stories.title: Berkadia Closes $219M Loan for Affordable Housing Rehab in Manhattan
stories.excerpt: Berkadia has closed a $219 million Fannie Mae loan to support the modernization of a 984-unit affordable housing community that was originally built in 1951 in Manhattan’s Washington Heights neighborhood. The 15-year permanent loan forms part of a $669 million capital structure that also includes an approximately $214 million subsidy from New York City and $94.5 million in federal and state historic tax credit equity. Located at 159-16 Harlem River Drive, the 11-acre public housing campus, dubbed Rangel Houses, includes eight high-rise buildings and serves more than 1,800 residents. Berkadia Affordable Housing’s Matthew Baptiste and Heather Olson arranged the financing on behalf of Genesis Companies, which plans to move forward with comprehensive renovations that will modernize the apartments and preserve their affordability. The financing was completed in partnership with the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA), the New York City Housing Development Corporation (HDC), and Goldman Sachs under NYCHA’s Permanent Affordability Commitment Together (PACT) program. “With the current volatility in the interest rate markets, Berkadia, in partnership with Fannie Mae, structured a creative financing plan that ensured the permanent loan proceeds were kept intact,” said Managing Director Heather Olson of Berkadia Affordable Housing in a statement. bullets: Berkadia closed $219M Fannie Mae permanent loan for 984-unit affordable housing modernization in Manhattan Washington Heights

stories.summary: Berkadia closed a $219 million Fannie Mae 15-year permanent loan supporting Genesis Companies' modernization of Rangel Houses, a 984-unit affordable housing community originally built in 1951 in Manhattan's Washington Heights neighborhood. The $669 million capital structure includes approximately $214 million in New York City subsidies and $94.5 million in federal and state historic tax credit equity. The 11-acre public housing campus comprises eight high-rise buildings serving more than 1,800 residents and will undergo comprehensive renovations to modernize apartments while preserving affordability.
stories.impact: Limited direct competitive impact on market-rate multifamily development in Manhattan. However, the scale of affordable housing capital deployment and NYC subsidy layering signals potential future zoning/regulatory pushes for below-market units in new multifamily projects in NYC submarkets, increasing development cost and complexity for future market-rate deals in affected neighborhoods.

stories.title: Recent Signing Brings Seattle Office Building to 96% Occupancy
stories.excerpt: The Swig Company’s Lake Union Building in Seattle now stands at 96% occupied after a recent lease agreement with an unnamed private equity firm for 5,000 square feet. Only one 3,800 square feet space remains on the building’s newly remodeled fifth floor. Located at 1700 Westlake Avenue N in Seattle’s South Lake Union neighborhood, Union Building is a seven-story, 98,000 sf office property that offers gorgeous lakefront views of Lake Union from every floor. The LEED Gold-certified building features a two-story parking garage and a 61-slip marina, a beautifully furnished outdoor patio facing the lake, a newly remodeled main lobby, a furnished floating dock for tenant use, and a bike storage room. The property also incorporates View dynamic glass windows, which automatically adjust in response to sunlight to help improve energy efficiency and occupant comfort. Jeff Huntington and Todd Battison of Kidder Mathews represented The Swig Company in the transaction. Ben Garrett and Jason Smith, also of Kidder Mathews, represented the tenant. The post Recent Signing Brings Seattle Office Building to 96% Occupancy appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lake Union Building (Seattle, South Lake Union) reached 96% occupancy after private equity firm leased 5K sf

stories.summary: The Swig Company's Lake Union Building in Seattle's South Lake Union neighborhood achieved 96% occupancy following a lease agreement with an unnamed private equity firm for 5,000 square feet. The seven-story, 98,000-square-foot LEED Gold-certified property at 1700 Westlake Avenue N features lakefront views, a two-story parking garage, 61-slip marina, and premium amenities. Only one 3,800-square-foot space remains on the newly remodeled fifth floor.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance. South Lake Union office strength reflects neighborhood resilience but does not signal new housing demand drivers. Conversely, office space strength may reduce conversion-to-multifamily opportunities in this submarket; monitor lease rates and downtime to assess future conversion economics.

stories.title: Greystone Supplies $47M Freddie Mac Loan on Illinois Multifamily Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Multifamily developer Grand Lifestyles has sealed $47 million of agency-backed debt to acquire an apartment complex in Chicago’s northern suburbs, Commercial Observer has learned. Greystone originated the Freddie Mac-backed loan for Grand Lifestyles’ acquisition of Foxboro Apartments in Wheeling, Ill., for $63.45 million. The 400-unit property was previously acquired by Marquette Companies in January 2020 for $54.25 million from Partnership Concepts in an off-market transaction before undergoing a renovation project that involved improvements to nearly half of the apartments. “Suburban Chicago continues to offer compelling acquisition opportunities, supported by steady rental demand and limited new multifamily supply,” Eric Rosenstock, senior managing director at Greystone, said in a statement. “Foxboro Apartments presented Grand Lifestyles with an opportunity to expand its portfolio with an established community in the Wheeling submarket, benefiting from recent capital improvements and strong underlying fundamentals.” Located at 470 Foxboro Drive, 28 miles northwest of Downtown Chicago, the 1977-built property has a mix of one- and two-bedroom apartments across nine buildings. Community amenities include a clubhouse, a fitness center, a swimming pool, a lounge, a business center, a dog park, tennis courts and a sand volleyball court. Grand Lifestyles also secured a $35.5 million Freddie Mac-backed loan from Greystone in September for the acquisition of another Chicago-area multifamily asset, the Ponds of Naperville in Naperville, Ill., CO first reported at the time. Grand Lifestyles did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Grand Lifestyles acquired Foxboro Apartments (400 units, Wheeling, Ill. suburbs) for $63.45M with $47M Freddie Mac loan
Previous owner Marquette Companies renovated nearly half of units since January 2020 acquisition; property generating strong underlying fundamentals
Chicago suburban multifamily demand and limited new supply supporting acquisition pricing; lender appetite for Freddie Mac financing remains robust
stories.summary: Multifamily developer Grand Lifestyles sealed $47 million of Freddie Mac-backed debt (originated by Greystone) to acquire Foxboro Apartments, a 400-unit property in Wheeling, Ill., 28 miles northwest of Downtown Chicago, for $63.45 million. The property was previously acquired by Marquette Companies in January 2020 for $54.25 million and underwent renovation improvements to nearly half of the apartments. Greystone noted that Suburban Chicago continues to offer compelling acquisition opportunities supported by steady rental demand and limited new multifamily supply.
stories.impact: Chicago suburban multifamily market fundamentals remain healthy: limited new supply, steady rental demand, and available agency financing support continued acquisition activity. Wheeling submarket in particular shows price appreciation (Marquette entry $54.3M in Jan 2020 → Grand Lifestyles $63.45M exit, implying ~17% appreciation in ~6 years plus unit renovations). Developers should accelerate Northern Illinois land acquisition before suburban cap rates compress further.

stories.title: U.K. Media Company Future Relocates East Coast HQ to Thor’s 25 West 39th Street
stories.excerpt: British media and publishing company Future is relocating its office to a spot near Midtown Manhattan’s Bryant Park, Commercial Observer has learned. The publisher of Live Science, Marie Claire and Homes & Gardens secured 13,000 square feet across the entire second floor of Thor Equities’ 25 West 39th Street, located one block south of Bryant Park. The 10-year lease agreement carries an asking rent of $70 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. Future was represented by Savills‘ Shay Bolton and Kirill Azovtsev, while Okada & Company’s Christopher Okada and Thomas Capuano negotiated on behalf of Thor. The building on 39th Street between Avenue of the Americas and Fifth Avenue is just a short stroll around the park from the publisher’s current East Coast headquarters at 130 West 42nd Street, also known as Bush Tower. Future signed a long-term deal for 16,000 square feet at the historic tower in 2021, according to Connect CRE. The publisher’s West Coast operations are headquartered in Los Angeles, according to its website. Thor’s West 39th Street tower recently secured another cross-border tenant in Century Cricket Centre, an Australia-based cricket concept that plans to soon open its first U.S. location at the property. Corporate tenants at the office building include content creation platform Spotter and art collective Tin Drum. Spokespeople for Future, Thor, Savills and Okada & Company did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Future (U.K. publisher: Live Science, Marie Claire, Homes & Gardens) relocated NYC HQ to 13K sf at 25 West 39th Street
10-year lease at $70/sf; company moved one block south from Bush Tower (130 West 42nd); represents office market stability near Bryant Park
Midtown Manhattan office leasing activity signals continued demand from media/publishing and creative tenants in Midtown submarkets
stories.summary: British media and publishing company Future relocated its East Coast headquarters from Bush Tower (130 West 42nd Street) to Thor Equities' 25 West 39th Street near Bryant Park in Midtown Manhattan. Future, publisher of Live Science, Marie Claire, and Homes & Gardens, secured 13,000 square feet on the entire second floor under a 10-year lease at an asking rent of $70 per square foot. Savills represented Future; Okada & Company represented Thor.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily impact; office-focused news. However, sustained Midtown Manhattan office leasing (especially by high-margin publishing/creative tenants at $70/sf) signals neighborhood stability and continued corporate presence, supporting neighborhood resilience and potential residential demand from office workers. Monitor office-to-residential conversion economics if office rents soften; currently, strong office demand argues against conversion opportunities.
